messages.subject: Re: QUESTION ABOUT GEOMORPH (procD.allometry
parts:
Hi Nicole,

some thoughts: your general approach is correct for analyzing your data.
However, the biological signal in your data seems to be "boarder-line"
in terms of whether or not you should consider different allometric
slopes for each group: the homogeneity of slopes test indicates
differences, but the effect is marginally not significant in your global
ANOVA table. For this reason, I recommend you run a pairwise comparison
of slopes using advanced.procD.lm(). This will allow you to evaluate the
strength and extension of slope divergence among your groups, and it
will help you decide whether your data justify using a model with
different slopes.

If you decide that it IS justified, interpretations should be made
focusing on the allometric slopes themselves, and not on the main
effects or two-way interactions, as is the case generally for more
complex interaction terms in ANOVAs.

As a side note, please use the geomorph googlegroup forum for future
communications and questions regarding geomorph:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/geomorph-r-package

This way users other than the geomorph developers can provide their
opinion and also benefit from this kind of questions. For reference, I
also recommend you search past conversations in the forum, as this kind
of topic has been treated before by other users.

Hope this helps!

Antigoni
